correctness.rationale: For n>=1,d>=2 over C, choose Q>d so all degree-d monomial torus weights are distinct. A monomial on sigma_2 must have first and second catalecticant rank <=2. First catalecticant excludes support >=3; for a two-variable monomial with both exponents >=2, second catalecticant has three divisors x_i^2,x_ix_j,x_j^2 and rank >=3. For d>=3 the surviving monomial points are exactly n+1 pure powers and n(n+1) tangent monomials x_i^(d-1)x_j, hence (n+1)^2; d=2 all binomial(n+2,2) monomials have symmetric rank <=2. Compactly supported C*-Euler localization on the projective secant gives the topological Euler numbers, subtracting chi(P^n)=n+1 gives the exact border-rank-two stratum. Independent monomial-exponent enumeration across n=1..5,d=2..7 reproduced the two counts; finite checks are not the proof. Crucially the claim concerns border rank, not ordinary symmetric rank.

value.rationale: Topological Euler characteristic of a basic singular secant variety is a natural global invariant. The sharp quadratic-vs-higher-degree transition holds uniformly across all n>=2 and is not a routine degree substitution; it converts flattening geometry into an exact secant-stratum topological count. The known n=1/d=2 boundary cases merely calibrate the substantive higher-dimensional theorem.

limitations: All claims over C; border rank not exact symmetric rank; only second secants and Euler characteristic, not Betti numbers.
